hypothesis: Under the single local rule of elementary cellular automaton rule 110, random initial configurations settle into one dominant periodic background (the 'ether') while other finite configurations embedded in it evolve as persistent localized structures with several distinct, exactly periodic signatures (different velocities), so one rule produces qualitatively different kinds of collective behavior.
pass_criterion: Pre-registered. (A) Background: there is a configuration on a 14-cell ring that rule 110 maps, after 7 steps, onto a rotation of itself (a spatially 14-periodic, temporally 7-periodic background), and in 20 independent random-initial-condition runs (density 0.5, cyclic lattice of 700 cells, 3000 steps) the mean fraction of cells whose 14-cell neighbourhood matches that background (any phase) over steps 1000-3000 is at least 0.50. (B) Structures: across the same runs, tracks of non-background cells that persist for at least 300 steps and are exactly periodic (the window around the track at time t equals the window at time t+p shifted by s cells, for 5 consecutive periods) exist with at least 3 distinct velocities s/p (pairwise differing by more than 0.05 cells/step). Both (A) and (B) must hold for 'supports'.
fail_criterion: Pre-registered. 'Refutes' if no 7-step periodic 14-cell background exists or the mean background fraction is below 0.25, or if fewer than 2 distinct exactly periodic localized-structure velocities are found across all runs. Anything between (background fraction 0.25-0.50, or exactly 2 velocities) is 'mixed'.
interpretation: Wolfram's statement is read as an existence claim about rule 110 (his stated example): the same cell rule, applied to different local configurations, yields (i) a regular periodic background and (ii) several distinct localized structures. 'Regular background' is operationalized as a spatially and temporally periodic configuration; 'localized structure' as a bounded cluster of non-background cells that persists and is exactly periodic up to a shift, so that its velocity s/p is a rational number. Distinct velocities are taken as evidence of 'different kinds of behavior'. No reinterpretation beyond this is needed; the test is computational and the 'dataset' is generated by analysis.py.
